name: TX-25
label: Safe R

key_factors: Williams holds an overwhelming financial edge: about $1.6M raised and $1.2M on hand versus roughly $5K for Sims
The district's R+11 lean combined with incumbency leaves little room for an upset
Sims's negative cash on hand signals a minimal campaign operation
Markets price the race around 96% Republican, and no polls or expert raters treat it as competitive
model.rationale: The incumbent's massive fundraising advantage and the district's strong Republican lean leave the underfunded challenger without a visible path; prediction markets and the absence of any competitive signals point the same way.
model.watch: A major influx of Democratic outside spending or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would be the main trigger for revision.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 25th District leans firmly Republican, and Representative Roger Williams is seeking another term with a substantial financial advantage. He has raised about $1.6 million and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Democrat Dione Sims has reported roughly $5,000 raised and negative cash on hand, indicating a minimal campaign operation. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Williams about a 96 percent chance of winning.

The national environment may favor Democrats in 2026, but an eleven-point Republican lean plus incumbency presents a steep hurdle. Williams is positioned to win by a wide margin; the main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling rather than any sign of competition. Sims would need significant outside investment and a major shift in the political climate to make this race competitive.
